claims.text: Interest while you wait is one month's interest, rounded half up to the cent, times the months you wait.
The balance when payments start is the loan balance plus the unpaid interest, exact to the cent.
With the toggle on, unpaid interest is added to the balance when payments start. With it off, interest keeps growing on the original balance only.
Months to pay off and total interest match a month-by-month schedule, rounded half up to the cent each month.
The payoff date is the start month plus the months to pay off, counted exactly.
The minimum payment is the smallest payment, to the cent, that pays off the loan in the years you chose.
The year-by-year sections add up to the totals and the balance ends at zero.
A rate of 0, a one-payment payoff and a 100-year payoff all work out exactly.
Messy typing never gives a wrong number, NaN or a crash.
A bad entry gets a calm message in plain words that names the field.
